preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner to deprecate the contract and set a malicious upgradedAddress
Contract must not already be deprecated (deprecated == false)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the deprecate() function with a malicious upgradedAddress that implements the UpgradedStandardToken interface but contains ERC721 non-conformant logic. This will cause the contract to redirect all token operations to the malicious contract, potentially breaking ERC20 compliance and allowing unauthorized transfers or state manipulation.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TetherToken contract has an upgrade mechanism that allows the owner to deprecate the contract and redirect all token operations to a new address. The vulnerability is that the owner can set a malicious upgraded contract that implements the required interface but contains non-conformant logic (e.g., ERC721 instead of ERC20). This breaks ERC20 compliance and could allow unauthorized operations.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner, deploy a malicious upgrade contract that implements the UpgradedStandardToken interface but contains ERC721 non-conformant logic, then call deprecate() to set this malicious contract as the upgradedAddress.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the contract owner. 2. Deploy a malicious upgrade contract that implements the required interface. 3. Call deprecate() on TetherToken with the malicious contract address. 4. Verify that deprecated is now true.
